The carbon monoxide concentrations reported in figure 51 for receptor number six show a trend which seems improbable. For 1977 and 1990, the one- and eight-hour concentrations are higher for the no-build case than for the build case in every instance except for the 1990 one-hour maximums where the reverse is indicated. This suggests an error in the last case.
The statement on page 80 that control of hydrocarbon emissions is required only in southeastern Wisconsin is incorrect. As indicated in Wisconsin Administrative Code NR 154.13, most of the hydrocarbon emission control rules apply throughout the state.
The question of growth stimulated by the Spur during the 10 years after its completion should have received further discussion in order to reconcile the statement on page 6 that the "Airport Spur and related development at and around the airport is expected to lead to more intensive use of the area with a significant heavier total traffic..." with the primary justification for the spur: to relieve traffic congestion on the local streets in the area.
We hope that the discussion and analysis of future aircraft emissions which, as mentioned on page 119, will appear in revisions to the airport master plan for General Mitchell Field, will include a discussion of any possible problems from receptor exposure to combined aircraft and automobile emissions.
Although the revised air quality report has not given a truly "comprehensive overview of the total transportation needs being served" as called for by Mr. Besadny in his letter to you of October 3, 1973, we are hopeful that this matter will receive further attention in these revisions to the Mitchell Field Master Plan.
We believe that all of the major points raised by the Department's Air Pollution Control Section and transmitted by Mr. Besadny with the above—mentioned letter have received a satisfactory response in the Air Quality Report for the Airport Spur and in DOT memorandums to file of January 25, 1974 and June 28, 1974 with the possible exception of questions related to airport development. We hope that these matters will also be dealt with in the airport master plan revisions.
Thank you for the opportunity to comment on the Airport Spur Air Quality Report.
Sincerely,
Bureau of Air Pollution Control and Solid Waste Management
Brooks Becker
Director
Enc.
